answer: An ocean research guild issues one voting ticket per attendee at simultaneous, witnessed check-ins. A relic exhibit serves as one venue; the ledger rejects an echo of any ticket using a round-specific nullifier. Wallets may be anonymous, but a thousand votes require a thousand people to attend, whom a farm must recruit and pay. This depends on honest witnesses, duplicate-person checks and a common schedule that prevents venue hopping. Proxy attendance and corrupt organizers remain risks; signatures alone do not prove unique people.
